novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2 (thm:sharp-transfer)
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed counterexample only says it “rules out the false condition E_{a,n}=o_P(1)” and identifies no published estimator, workflow, or bibkey that actually relies on that condition.

soundness_flags.label: Lemma 1 (lem:boundary-likelihood)
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed supremum uses x≥n^{-B}, but B is declared as a subsample index set rather than a positive cutoff exponent, so this domain is not defined.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (thm:oracle-preservation) and E_{a,n}
soundness_flags.one_line: The boundary chart fixes π_a(0)=0 while E_{a,n} takes a pointwise supremum over {π_a(x)≤u_{a,n}}, which includes x=0 and hence contains the undefined ratio \widehatπ_a(0)/π_a(0).

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 6–7, equations (7)–(13) and Theorem 3.1; pp. 12–13, Section 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives the known-propensity fixed-quantile infinitely divisible/Gaussian limit under regular variation; Section 6 says the theory assumes a known propensity and threshold, then discusses a well-specified parametric propensity fit as a practical approach.

The paper uses nonparametric propensity estimation plus separate quantile minimizations and reports root-n consistency, asymptotic normality, and semiparametric efficiency under its regular QTE setup.
The article establishes efficiency of inverse weighting with a nonparametric estimated propensity score for the average treatment effect, not a weak-overlap QTE result.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The checked manuscript studies regular parametric binary-response propensity fits and normalized IPW estimation of the ATE; Theorem 4.1 gives normalized Gaussian or irregular limits for that mean-type statistic.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the pointwise E_{a,n} by a well-defined essential supremum over an explicitly truncated positive-propensity tail band, state the positive cutoff exponent, and prove that the learner's boundary-chart parameterization controls the excluded extreme region.

Make thm:sharp-transfer a generic-class sharpness theorem with a clearly stated practical class of learned propensity procedures, or identify a named published workflow that uses the weaker fixed-window criterion and formulate the strict failure against it.

Add a corollary comparing the feasible procedure directly with the anchor's parametric plug-in discussion and quantify the explicit enlargement from its parametric regime to the boundary-power sieve class.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two undefined boundary-domain expressions and anchor the sharp-transfer negative result to a concrete comparator, then continue this field-tier angle to Stage 0.
